messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-#87421 - routing.latency.p99 spike in us-west - auto-escalation enabled

sam (oncall): seeing it, paging now. grabbing basic graphs.
jordan (engineer): on it, running a quick tail on proxy logs. looks like short-lived 503s from dedicated-proxy-02 cluster
leah (sre): telemetry shows a very tight 30s window with requests queuing on proxy layer, then everything falls back to normal. could be warmup or a synthetic canary blip

incidentbot: Alert auto-ack policy: soft-ack applied by oncall. Will suppress duplicate pages for 5m unless severity increases.

sam (oncall): soft-acked to avoid wakeups, leaving channel for correlation. if it persists i'll escalate.
jordan (engineer): grep output snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T12:01:03Z] proxy: accept conn id=1245 latency=120ms status=200
[2026-03-15T12:01:12Z] proxy: backend=dedicated-proxy-02 err=connect reset status=503
[2026-03-15T12:01:18Z] proxy: accept conn id=1250 latency=95ms status=200
```
mike (oncall): looks like single backend flaking, maybe a transient driver hiccup. rolling restart of dedicated-proxy-02 would be heavy; can we drain just that node?
jordan (engineer): starting a quick drain on dedicated-proxy-02 now, stepping down from LB rotation. expecting in ~20s.
leah (sre): checking customer impact: APM traces show no errors propagated to front-end transactions; only internal retries. marking impact as likely none for now.
sam (oncall): good. keeping PD in soft-silence. if incidentbot sees >3 failures in 2m it'll re-awaken.

incidentbot: automated metric: routing.latency.p99 = 420ms (threshold 400ms) at peak, returned to baseline 210ms 45s later.
jordan (engineer): drain finished, kube node cordon succeeded, connections are healthy. logs look quiet.
mike (oncall): pinging the customer-facing health check endpoints, all green.
sam (oncall): i'll flip the page to resolved once we confirm no recurrence in the next 5m. anybody see related alerts (kv-cache, autoscaler)?
leah (sre): kv-cache ops are normal. autoscaler didn't kick. seems isolated to that proxy instance. adding a follow-up ticket to investigate driver/firmware mismatch on that host.
jordan (engineer): filing ticket INF-3241 with logs and node id. attaching the small diagnostic bundle.
sam (oncall): ack, thanks. incidentbot, note: manual soft-ack held; resolution pending postmortem.

incidentbot: Page resolved by auto-suppression timeout and operator confirmation. No PD re-escalation.
mike (oncall): :thumbsup: little noisy synthetic or infra flake. no customer impact.
leah (sre): I'll own the postmortem. short-term follow-up: schedule a non-disruptive kernel/driver upgrade trial on the node pool and add a canary that exercises connection churn.
sam (oncall): thanks team. closing thread in 10m if no recurrence. leaving notes in oncall-runbook about soft-ack pattern for low-confidence flaps.
jordan (engineer): +1. also adding a metric alert to track single-node failure correlation to reduce noise.

mike (oncall): done, marking as resolved in PD and adding a runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/soft-ack-handling
sam (oncall): good work everyone.

-- end of thread --
